For each qualifying orderkey, direct-array lookup into orders
Direct array lookup: row_id = c_custkey - 1 (dense 1-based PKs)
steps.notes: c_name decoded only for final 100 rows; c_custkey already known from o_custkey

steps.description: Sort ~15K result tuples and take top 100
steps.notes: std::partial_sort or nth_element+sort for top 100 from ~15K rows

steps.description: Decode c_name only for final 100 result rows

join_order.notes: Use orders_o_orderkey_lookup for O(1) lookup per qualifying orderkey

parallelism.partition: partition orderkey range across threads, each thread collects local qualifying set, then merge
parallelism.notes: Subquery iterates ~15M groups over ~60M l_quantity values — parallelize this. Remaining steps operate on ~15K rows, single-threaded is fine.

indexes.layout: header: uint64_t num_entries; body: interleaved uint32_t[num_entries*2] as [start, count] pairs
header: uint64_t num_entries; body: int32_t[num_entries] where arr[orderkey] = row_id, -1 if missing

aggregation_notes: SUM(l_quantity) is computed during the subquery grouped scan. The GROUP BY in the outer query has ~15K groups keyed by o_orderkey (which uniquely determines all other group-by columns). Since sum_qty is already computed per orderkey in the subquery, no further aggregation hash table is needed.
